subject: Acme Payments: request for third-party processing chain + evidence pull
messages:
From: Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@acmepayments.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmepayments.com, security@acmepayments.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: list of subprocessors, dataflows, and evidence package

Hi Irene,

Hope you’re well. As part of our vendor onboarding we need a complete declaration of Redwood’s third-party processing chain that could touch Acme Payments customer data. Specifically we need:

- A current subprocessor roster (names, country, purpose) covering storage, telemetry, caching, and 3rd-party monitoring.
- A high-level dataflow diagram showing cross-border hops and any encryption-in-transit assurances.
- Evidence of KMS/HSM controls and a recent attestation for key management.
- Any DPA addendum or required language for our procurement team.

Can you provide the above within 5 business days? We’re aiming to complete our security review before our launch window. I attached a short questionnaire the security team filled out to help.

Thanks,
Lisa Monroe
Director, Vendor Security
Acme Payments
Attachment: acme_subprocessor_questionnaire.pdf
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: list of subprocessors, dataflows, and evidence package

Folks — forwarding Acme’s ask. Timeline: 5 business days. Priority: procurement lift for launch.

Quick notes:
- They want the full roster + dataflow diagram + KMS attestation + DPA addendum.
- I’m happy to coordinate the external response and drop the deliverables into Drive/DocuSign, but need legal + security sign-off on the addendum language and the attestation PDF.

Can each of you confirm what you can own? I’ll assemble the packet and send a single reply to Lisa to avoid multiple inbound threads.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: list of subprocessors, dataflows, and evidence package

Irene — I can own the DPA addendum wording and sign-off.

Action items from legal:
1) Share current subprocessor roster (we’ll redline only if there are new restricted countries or escrow requirements).
2) We can draft a one-page DPA addendum focused on: permitted subprocessors, DSAR handling, transit encryption language, and onshore fallback commitments.
3) We’ll need Ben to confirm the KMS attestation doc and any supporting certificates.

Timeline: I’ll put a draft addendum in the Drive folder by tomorrow EOD (link preferred). If procurement wants DocuSign, Lauren can trigger the envelope after we agree on language.

-KP
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: list of subprocessors, dataflows, and evidence package

On Wed, Jun 30, 2026 at 11:02 AM kimberly.park@redwood.ai wrote:
> Irene — I can own the DPA addendum wording and sign-off.

I’ll pull the KMS/HSM attestation and the recent key rotation log export.
Current plan:
- KMS attestation PDF (kms-attestation-2026-06.pdf) — includes HSM provider, monthly audit summary, and onshore key escrow options.
- Redacted key rotation log (redacted-key-rotation-2026-06.csv) — redacted for entropy but shows rotation dates + executor roles.
- Short note on encryption in transit (we use TLS 1.3, mTLS on internal links + AWS Transit/GCP interconnect where applicable).

I’ll upload the artifacts to the Drive link this morning and flag any items with export control considerations.

Ben Carter
Head of Production Security
Redwood Inference
Attachments (to be uploaded): kms-attestation-2026-06.pdf, redacted-key-rotation-2026-06.csv

Lauren Bishop

Deliverables included (attachments):
- Redwood subprocessor roster (storage, telemetry, caching, monitoring) — table inside the cover PDF.
- dataflow-map-acme.png — high-level diagram showing transit hops and onshore fallback paths.
- kms-attestation-2026-06.pdf — KMS/HSM attestation and a summary of key control processes.
- dpa_addendum_draft.docx — one-page DPA addendum we propose for quick procurement acceptance.
- acme_subprocessor_questionnaire.pdf — completed answers to your questionnaire.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly will finalize any legal tweaks to the addendum today — we’ll send a DocuSign envelope if you confirm that flow works.
2) Lauren will post the archive to the HubSpot deal and trigger DocuSign once we have sign-off.
3) Ben will be available for any technical follow-ups on KMS/HSM controls or to set up a short call if your security team wants to validate specific controls.

If you’d like a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow morning PST to go through the artifact package live, we can set that up.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference
